sections.h2: Which sale route suits a house in Statesboro?
sections.html:
Statesboro owners have three ways out: hand the house to a listing agent, find a buyer unaided, or accept a cash price from a purchaser who takes the property with all its flaws. Two facts decide most cases. One is the cost of the work the house needs. The other is whether a tenant holds a lease.

  • A listing earns the top price on a tidy, updated house if you can live with open houses and a buyer's mortgage process.
  • Going solo saves the commission and hands you the paperwork, the questions and the negotiating.
  • A cash sale draws landlords, heirs and anyone on a clock, since no repairs or lender conditions stand in the way.

The city covers only about 15 square miles and most of its homes are rented. Deal with the tenant question first, because it narrows the field of buyers.

sections.h2: How many Statesboro homes are owner-occupied, and what do they cost?
sections.html:
Roughly one Statesboro home in five houses its owner. Census estimates for 2020 to 2024 show 22.1 percent owner occupancy among 12,545 households, and the bureau's mid-2025 estimate of 35,366 residents compares with 33,438 counted in 2020.

An investor will anchor on that $944 rent and ask what a unit could earn, so a house with paying tenants already in place can look better to a landlord than to a family.

sections.h2: How did Statesboro become a college and industrial town?
sections.html:
Statesboro is the seat of Bulloch County, and the county's own planning document says the area grew in the late 1800s on railroads that hauled out timber, Sea Island cotton and naval stores. The city was incorporated in 1903. By 1906 local leaders were asking the state to place a small teacher's college there, and that school became Georgia Southern University.

The same plan treats the university, now enrolling 25,500 students, as the largest single force shaping modern Statesboro. It describes an industrial surge in the 1990s, when Wal-Mart, Briggs and Stratton and Viracon settled in the county's industrial park. Later the Development Authority bought land along Interstate 16, and the county and city extended water and sewer lines to the Bruce Yawn Commerce Park on the US 301 corridor.

Agriculture has not gone away. The plan counts over 206,000 farm acres in Bulloch County devoted to row crops, livestock and poultry, with newer ventures such as sweet onions and satsuma citrus. Outlying houses may have a field or a poultry house for a neighbor.

sections.h2: Who tends to sell a Statesboro house quickly?
sections.html:
These sellers usually hold a property that needs cash or patience before a mortgage buyer would consider it. Around a university, the trigger is often the lease calendar or a landlord ready to exit.

  • Landlords whose tenants are still under lease, or whose unit sat vacant after students left.
  • Heirs carrying a Bulloch County house while the estate and the deed are sorted out.
  • Borrowers behind on payments who would rather sell than face a foreclosure sale.
  • Sellers with a failing roof, aging plumbing or a cracked slab that an appraiser would mark down.

With a tenant inside, pull out the signed lease and note the deposit before you weigh any offer. Whoever steps into the lease will ask for both, and the deposit must be credited or handed over at closing.

sections.h2: What does Bulloch County do with property tax, and what matters at a sale?
sections.html:
Value is fixed as of January 1, and the tax falls on 40 percent of it, after exemptions, at each taxing body's millage rate. Bulloch's tax page describes a local twist: the assessors, and not the tax commissioner, receive returns and homestead applications.

  • Someone who bought in the previous year owes a real property return by April 1, and a late one can draw a 10 percent penalty.
  • A new owner whose PT-61 was filed with the tax paid can skip the return if nothing was split off or built afterward.
  • A letter to the assessors within 45 days of the notice starts an appeal of a changed value. If they keep the number, the case moves to the Board of Equalization, or the owner can choose arbitration.
  • The county's page lists the standard $2,000 homestead exemption and several age and disability breaks, and it describes a deferral option for owners 62 and over whose gross income is $15,000 or less.
  • Land in bona fide farm use may be assessed at 30 percent in place of 40 in exchange for a 10 year commitment.

Bulloch is missing from the state's roster of counties with a homestead valuation freeze. The state's county fact sheet sets December 20 as the default payment date and lets a county move it, so ask the Bulloch tax commissioner which date applies to your parcel.

sections.h2: What happens at the courthouse when a Statesboro house changes hands?
sections.html:
The Bulloch County Clerk of Superior Court will not record a deed until the state's transfer tax is settled. By default the seller owes it, and the Department of Revenue posts the rate and the exemptions on its transfer tax page. Security deeds and their releases skip the PT-61 altogether.

Whoever runs your closing normally submits the PT-61 electronically and settles the tax from your proceeds. For tax questions, the county offices share an annex on North Main Street downtown, open weekdays from 8 AM to 5 PM. Bring the parcel number, since the assessors and the tax commissioner keep separate files.

sections.h2: How do Statesboro's highways and new employers affect demand?
sections.html:
Interstate 16 and US 301 are the arteries. The county plan expects Bulloch to feel the pull of the Hyundai Metaplant rising in neighboring Bryan County, and it names Aspen Aerogels, announced in February 2022 with 250 advanced manufacturing jobs, as the first of five industries heading to the county. Georgia Highway 67 and the I-16 interchange zone are marked for denser growth where utilities will reach.

Everyday amenities appear in the plan as well. The S and S Greenway runs 3.1 paved miles along the old Savannah and Statesboro railway bed, and Mill Creek Regional Park covers 223 acres and has hosted up to 20,000 visitors in a day. Workers report an average commute of 22.9 minutes. A good description of your house leads with distance to campus, access to I-16 and the rent a landlord could expect.

sections.h2: What should a Statesboro owner do before taking an offer?
sections.html:
1. Look up your parcel with the Bulloch assessors and confirm the value and any exemption on record.
  2. If tenants are inside, keep the lease, the deposit figure and their contact information together.
  3. Call the tax commissioner for the balance and the due date, and find out if your lender pays from escrow.
  4. Put an as-is cash price beside a listing agent's opinion of value and weigh the gap against repair costs and carrying costs.
  5. Choose who will run the closing, clear liens, file the PT-61 and record the deed.

Tax questions belong with the county offices. Estate and lien questions belong with the closing attorney.

faqs.q: How quickly can a Statesboro house close for cash?
faqs.a: Timing depends on title and on the buyer. A house with an open estate or an unpaid lien takes longer, because the title search sets the pace and the deed cannot be recorded until the transfer tax is paid and liens are cleared.

faqs.q: Does the seller or the buyer owe the Georgia transfer tax in Statesboro?
faqs.a: The seller owes it unless the sales contract says the buyer will pay. The Department of Revenue's transfer tax page gives the rate, which is applied to the sale price.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Statesboro house while tenants live in it?
faqs.a: Yes. The buyer can take the house subject to the lease, or you can end the lease under its own terms before closing. Keep the written lease and the deposit record, since both are needed at closing.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to contest a Bulloch County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the date on the notice of change, in writing, to the Board of Tax Assessors. The appeal can rest on taxability, value or uniformity, and it cannot be a complaint about the amount of tax.

faqs.q: What if I inherited the Statesboro house?
faqs.a: You need clear authority before any buyer can close, and the estate representative has to sign. Ask the closing attorney what documents the title company will require, then set the closing date.
